properties.statement:
`loop_status.sync` REPORTS `in_step` WHILE LIVE NODES ARE ABSENT FROM THE EXPORT, AND NOTHING ELSE IN THE LOOP REPORTS THEM EITHER — so the only recoverable copy can be stale with every signal green. Reported by dragon Boss (`e41c6fb8`) 2026-08-16 against the StoryFlow fleet graph; REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY in reflow2's own session the same day.

⚠️ THEIR DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE FINDING. They hypothesised a measure-itself check that 'can only ever agree with itself'. The mechanism is real but it is NOT a bug: `sync_debt.rs:199` takes a cheap gate — `if &found == expected` where `found` is COMPUTED from the file on disk and `expected` is the hash recorded when THIS graph last wrote it — and returns `in_step` via `bare()`, which hardcodes `nodes_not_here_total: 0` (`sync_debt.rs:272`). So on that path the count is structurally always zero, exactly as they guessed. BUT `ver:the-record-moved-is-surfaced` names as a COVERED, TESTED property: 'that ordinary unexported work is NEVER reported, which is the property the whole design rests on.' The feature answers ONE question — has the SHARED RECORD moved ahead of me — and answers it correctly. `req:a-seat-learns-the-record-moved-before-it-writes` is about ANOTHER SEAT's work arriving, never about this seat's work leaving.

⭐ SO THE DEFECT IS NOT IN sync. IT IS THAT NOTHING COVERS THE OTHER DIRECTION. `behind` detects 'someone else exported work I do not have'. There is no state, on `sync` or anywhere on `loop_status`, for 'I hold work I have not exported' — and `in_step`, in a field called `sync`, is read as if it were both. The word is doing damage the code is not.

MY OWN REPRODUCTION, which is why this is recorded rather than filed as their claim: at the start of this session `loop_status.sync` reported `state: in_step` for `docs/design/reflow2.json` with `expected == found` and `nodes_not_here_total: 0`. A direct diff of the live store against that same committed export then found TWO TemporalFacts present live and absent from the file — `fact:defect-import-materialises-defaults-so-a-restored-graph-reads-as-changed` and `fact:defect-the-latent-surface-never-re-probes-after-a-cli-restore`, an earlier session's entire triage of music_graph F23 and F24. The previous session's handoff had recorded, on the strength of that same green, 'Graph in_step with the committed export, nothing behind.' It was not. Two facts were one machine failure from gone, and the only reason they survived is that this session exported for an unrelated reason.

COST, and it is asymmetric: the loss is SILENT, the graph keeps answering normally, and it becomes visible only when the machine does. dragon Boss's framing is the one to keep — a session that checks sync, sees `in_step`, and stands down reasonably believes its work is durable.

CHEAPEST HONEST FIX, and it is theirs: report the LIVE node/edge count beside the export's on every sync entry. It needs no export build (the file is already parsed and `count_nodes` is cheap), it preserves the property the design rests on, and it converts an unfalsifiable green into a readable one. A caller today cannot tell 'I compared and they match' from 'I compared the file to its own recorded hash', and those are different claims with the same output.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a count comparison alone is sufficient (equal counts with different ids would still pass), and whether the right home is `sync` or a separate loop debt class.
